text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto unveils major policy initiative aimed at expanding breadth and depth of Japan's relationship with ASEAN nations.
- Leader of biggest delegation of American congressmen to visit China rules out possibility of U.S. decision to grant China permanent most-favoured nation trading status this year.
- UN security staff find fourth letter bomb sent to the UN bureau of Arabic-language newspaper, a day after letter bomb exploded at paper's London office.
- A Thai MP proposes awarding pick-up trucks as lucky draw prizes to lure truant legislators back to notoriously ill-attended parliament.
- In yet another sign Singapore electronics industry is climbing slowly out of doldrums, disk drive majors report tight product supplies.
- Thai cabinet approves proposal to let private sector set up funds to buy ailing housing projects as part of measures to alleviate glut in property market.
- Stockbroking houses and property agencies still paying good bonuses despite last year's slower economic growth.
- Asian telecommunication companies meet in Hawaii next week to discuss matters of mutual concern, with talks expected to be dominated by American rate-cutting proposal that could cost them billions.
- Singapore International Monetary Exchange members see tough year ahead with commissions under pressure in the face of falling turnover.
- Malaysian firms win contract worth some 5 billion ringgit for massive Bakun dam project.
- Jardine Fleming foresees lukewarm upturn for Singapore share market this year.
